title: Kripke semantics for intuitionistic propositions

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic (ILLC report PP-2006-25; ESSLLI 2005 lectures)
based_on.pages: Section 3.3 printed pp. 15–17, Definition 3, persistence, Figure 2, Definition 8, Theorem 9.

summary: Interpret intuitionistic proofs in persistent ordered models and use small countermodels to separate them from classical reasoning.
abstract: An atom may be unverified now and verified at a later extension of the available information. Kripke models describe this situation using ordered worlds and require every verified atom to remain verified. An implication must remain valid at all later worlds, while a negation rules out later verification of its subject. We prove that every intuitionistic natural-deduction proof respects these conditions, that substitution and restriction to all extensions preserve the interpretation, and that a single world recovers ordinary Boolean truth. Two small models then show why excluded middle, double-negation elimination, and one direction of De Morgan’s law can fail even though truth tables validate them.
